plotSections.title: Ord surveys the silent boat
bullets: With See Invisibility active, Ord sees Gerk and Sylan wrestling near the closed spectral door while Dana looks concerned and confused.
Two crew members wander the deck bumping into each other and silently trying to call out.
All visible activity remains completely soundless.
Where Gerk opened his portal, faint glowing edge-lines and ghostly city passerby fade quickly and are nearly gone when Ord investigates.

plotSections.title: Contact through blind eye speech
bullets: Ord’s spoken words still do not carry; his persuasion check of 15 lets him calmly steady Sylan and Gerk, who notice his oily silhouette.
Sylan uses a token of blind eye speech to whisper with Ord and confirm he can see them.
Gerk admits through the token that he opened the door.
The token requires pointing and whispering to activate, but Gerk can reply directly to whispers sent to him.

plotSections.title: Investigating the spectral door
bullets: The spectral door floats over and slightly behind Gerk, shut and frameless, resembling Gerk’s shield-door but more functional.
With guidance, Gerk’s investigation total of 18 reveals it is not a real door but protective magic with no portal or opening capability.
Gerk and Sylan’s hands pass through it into thicker-feeling air with no physical resistance or effect.
Gerk wildly swings through the door without changing it.
Ord’s attempt to turn a doorknob also passes straight through.
The DM notes passing through the spectral door would not simply restore sight or hearing.

plotSections.title: Debate over dispelling the effect
bullets: Sylan suggests dispel magic may be their strongest available tool but warns about their poor track record with it.
The party fears dispelling the wrong magic could drop them to their deaths, noting Dana is the one who could most likely prevent that.
Ord proposes casting zone of truth and intentionally failing the save so any spoken fix ideas must be truthful.

chronologicalEvents: Ord sees Dana, confused crew, the spectral door, and fading portal residue on the silent boat.
Ord investigates the fading glowing lines, but they are almost gone.
Ord steadies Sylan and Gerk with a persuasion check of 15.
Sylan uses blind eye speech to confirm Ord can see the party.
Gerk says he opened the door.
Gerk sees the shut floating spectral door behind him.
Gerk investigates the door with guidance and totals 18.
Gerk learns the spectral door is fake protective magic, not a real opening.
Gerk, Sylan, and Ord all find their hands pass through the spectral door without effect.
Gerk wildly swings through the door to no avail.
Ord tries and fails to grasp the spectral doorknob.
The party debates using dispel magic versus the risk of falling.
Ord proposes a zone of truth workaround to force truthful solution ideas.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian Doorman and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: Admits he opened the door.
Investigates the spectral door with guidance for a total of 18.
Determines it is fake protective magic with no real portal or opening function.
His hands and arms pass through the spectral door without affecting it.
Uses a token of blind eye speech to communicate with Ord.
Casts guidance on Gerk’s door investigation.
Pushes Gerk to investigate the door as Doorman and tests the spectral door with him.
Warns that dispel magic is powerful but risky given the party’s past results.
Still sees the invisible silent scene through See Invisibility.
Investigates the fading portal residue and steadies Sylan and Gerk with persuasion 15.
Confirms via blind eye speech that he can see the party.
Fails to physically interact with the spectral door.
Proposes using zone of truth and intentionally failing the save to extract truthful fix ideas.
Remains on the boat looking concerned and confused when Ord can see her.
The party says she is the one most likely able to stop them if dispelling the magic causes a fall.

Spectral Door.existing: A mysterious spectral door resembling Gerk's shield form.
notes: Floats over and slightly behind Gerk, fully shut and frameless.
Resembles Gerk’s shield-door but looks more functional and less shield-like.
Investigation reveals it is fake protective magic, not a real door with portal capability.
Hands pass through it into slightly thicker air without physical effect.
Passing through it does not simply restore normal sight or hearing.
openQuestions: Should the party dispel the spectral door’s magic?

Doorway.existing: A fixed supernatural passage between locations.
notes: Gerk’s earlier opened portal left fading glowing edge-lines and ghostly city visions.
That residue is separate from the floating spectral door and nearly gone by the time Ord inspects it.

Abel.existing: Surviving-and-revived crew member and the boat's helmsman.
notes: Visible to Ord as one of two confused crew members silently wandering the deck.
Sylan uses it to whisper with Ord when normal speech fails.
Requires pointing and whispering to activate.
Gerk can reply to whispers sent to him without needing to activate it himself.
